hints.title: Store Category Aggregation
hints.text: Aggregate product quantities by store and category to determine category-level inventory counts.

hints.title: Category Disparity Calculation
hints.text: Compute the difference between the most stocked category and least stocked category per store.

hints.title: Threshold Filtering and Join
hints.text: Filter for stores with multiple categories exhibiting an inventory disparity of at least 50 units.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH store_category_quantities AS (
    SELECT 
        store_id,
        category,
        SUM(quantity) AS cat_qty
    FROM inventory
    GROUP BY store_id, category
),
store_imbalances AS (
    SELECT 
        store_id,
        MAX(cat_qty) AS max_category_qty,
        MIN(cat_qty) AS min_category_qty,
        MAX(cat_qty) - MIN(cat_qty) AS imbalance
    FROM store_category_quantities
    GROUP BY store_id
    HAVING COUNT(category) >= 2 AND (MAX(cat_qty) - MIN(cat_qty)) >= 50
)
SELECT 
    s.store_id,
    s.store_name,
    s.location,
    i.max_category_qty,
    i.min_category_qty,
    i.imbalance
FROM store_imbalances i
JOIN stores s ON i.store_id = s.store_id
ORDER BY i.imbalance DESC, s.store_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Two-level group aggregation followed by threshold filter and store join.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries per category create quadratic joins on large inventories.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping by store and category condenses rows before calculating extremes.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use CTEs to compute category totals and compare maximum versus minimum.

import pandas as pd

def find_stores_with_inventory_imbalance(stores: pd.DataFrame, inventory: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    cat_sum = inventory.groupby(['store_id', 'category'])['quantity'].sum().reset_index()
    
    grouped = cat_sum.groupby('store_id').agg(
        max_category_qty=('quantity', 'max'),
        min_category_qty=('quantity', 'min'),
        cat_count=('category', 'count')
    ).reset_index()
    
    grouped['imbalance'] = grouped['max_category_qty'] - grouped['min_category_qty']
    valid = grouped[(grouped['cat_count'] >= 2) & (grouped['imbalance'] >= 50)]
    
    res = valid.merge(stores, on='store_id', how='inner')
    res = res.sort_values(by=['imbalance', 'store_id'], ascending=[False, True])
    return res[['store_id', 'store_name', 'location', 'max_category_qty', 'min_category_qty', 'imbalance']]
